title: U.S. stocks see 3rd-largest weekly single-stock outflow since 2008: BofA (SPY:NYSEARCA)
source_used: Seeking Alpha text, read on TradingView
key_facts: Institutional investors sold $11 billion of US single stocks last week, the third-largest single-stock outflow in Bank of America's data history.
Technology shares led the selling; the tech sector fund's weekly outflow was its fourth-largest since 2008, and four-week average tech flows turned negative for the first time since July.
Outflows hit nine of 11 sectors; materials and real estate were the only sectors with net inflows.
Institutional clients sold single stocks for a second consecutive week, while hedge funds and retail investors were net buyers, the first retail inflows since late July.
Clients put $3.2 billion into equity ETFs for the 15th straight week, favouring value and blend funds over growth.
The note was written by Bank of America strategist Jill Carey Hall.
quote_evidence: Institutional investors logged massive single-stock outflows last week, dumping $11B in U.S. equities in a tech-heavy retreat that marked the third-largest single-stock outflow in Bank of America's data history.
Selling across the market was overwhelmingly led by technology XLK shares.
why_it_matters_hint: Large institutions sold single stocks, led by tech, while retail and hedge funds bought; one bank's flow data.
event_date: week to early Oct 2026 (note reported 7 Oct 2026)
